title: Containerizer: organization scans
description: Scheduled organization scans (containerizer worker), the worker process and the machine it runs on. docs/scheduled-scans.md

panels.title: Worker
panels.description: Is Prometheus reaching the worker's metrics endpoint?

panels.title: Scans running
panels.description: Runs in progress now.

panels.title: Runs waiting
panels.description: Queued runs no worker has picked up yet. Stays above 0 when the worker is busy or stopped.

panels.title: Since the last successful run
panels.description: Time since a run of the selected scans last finished. A weekly scan should stay under 8 days.

panels.title: Next run in
panels.description: Until the next scheduled run of the selected scans (UTC schedule on the admin pages).

panels.title: Failed runs (7 days)
panels.description: Runs that stopped with an error (organization or output repository unreachable, worker crashed).

panels.title: Current or latest run: progress
panels.description: Repositories processed so far out of those the run has to process.

panels.title: Repositories by state
panels.description: enabled: processed at every run; disabled_automatic: skipped by the scan, with a reason (Dockerfile, no application code, stale, ...); disabled_admin: disabled on the admin pages; removed: no longer in the organization.

panels.title: Repositories by latest result
panels.description: What happened to each repository the last time a run reached it.

panels.title: Repositories processed
panels.description: Repositories finished per interval, by result.

panels.title: Time per repository
panels.description: Fetch, analyze, build and run, gate and push of one repository (last hour).

panels.title: Clones and pulls
panels.description: The first run clones; later runs only fetch the newest commit.

panels.title: Time in git
panels.description: Share of the time spent cloning and pulling.

panels.title: LLM calls
panels.description: LLM calls in the selected time range (answered, cached and failed).

panels.title: Tokens in
panels.description: Prompt tokens sent to the LLM in the selected time range.

panels.title: Tokens out
panels.description: Tokens the LLM answered with in the selected time range.

panels.title: Estimated cost
panels.description: Estimated LLM cost in the selected time range: list prices of the Claude models, or CONTAINERIZER_LLM_PRICE_INPUT/_OUTPUT for a self-hosted LLM (0 when not set).

panels.title: LLM-heavy mode
panels.description: Scans with LLM-heavy mode on (the scan's setting, Ask the LLM, and CZ_LLM_HEAVY in appliance.env). Off by default.

panels.title: LLM tokens by feature
panels.description: Tokens in and out per interval, by what the call was for: assessment, build-diagnosis, dev-database, platform-migration, sandbox-tester.

panels.title: LLM calls by feature and result
panels.description: Calls per interval. cached: answered from the cache, no tokens used; failed: the LLM could not be reached or gave no valid answer.

panels.title: Estimated cost by repository
panels.description: The repositories that cost the most LLM time in the selected range.

panels.title: Tokens by repository and feature
panels.description: Tokens in and out in the selected range, per repository and feature.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of all CPUs by mode (builds and image scans run in Docker on this machine). iowait or steal staying high means slow disks or an overcommitted VM.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: Load average against the number of CPUs.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Used = total - available (what the kernel can give new work without swapping).

panels.title: Disk space used
panels.description: data: the worker's clones and work folders; docker: images and build cache (prune with docker system prune). Full disks are the most common reason a scan fails.

panels.title: Disk I/O
panels.description: Reads up, writes down.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Clones, base images and pushes. In up, out down.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU of the worker and of the tools it starts (the builds themselves run in Docker: see the machine's CPU).
